uncited: It builds on [Minkowski Sum Boundary Rendering via Primitive Culling](14570-minkowski-sum-boundary-rendering-via-primitive-culling.md) by extending the primitive culling concept to a full volumetric voxelization pipeline.
- **Inputs:** Two polyhedra $A$ and $B$, defined by their triangle facets $F_A, F_B$, vertices $V_A, V_B$, and edges $E_A, E_B$.
- **Outputs:** A 3D grid of binary voxels representing the solid Minkowski sum $A \oplus B$, and a surface voxelization derived from the exterior boundary.
- **Voxel Grid:** A 3D array of binary values (0 or 1) stored exclusively on the GPU.
Each voxel represents a unit volume cell.
Translating a triangle in $F_A$ by a vector in $V_B$ (Triangle Primitive).
Translating a triangle in $F_B$ by a vector in $V_A$ (Triangle Primitive).
Sweeping an edge in $E_A$ along an edge in $E_B$ (Quadrilateral Primitive).
Identify and remove surface primitives that lie entirely inside the Minkowski sum and will not contribute to the final boundary.
This generates an initial solid voxelization.
Employ a fast flood fill algorithm on the voxel grid to identify all outside voxels.
- **Memory Complexity:** Volumetric data is stored and computed exclusively on the GPU.
- **When not to use:** When a precise boundary representation (B-rep) is required instead of a voxelized approximation.

The flood fill step effectively distinguishes the interior (voxels not reached by the flood fill from the outside) from the exterior, which is the standard method for ensuring a watertight solid without holes in voxelization algorithms. Thus, the claim is fully supported by the text.
